data.value: Load of the processor and the graphics cards, memory use, free disk space and temperatures, from Windows or from a sensor program (HWiNFO, MSI Afterburner, LibreHardwareMonitor); the processor temperature only from a sensor program.

data.value: Start HWiNFO, Afterburner or LibreHardwareMonitor to see it
data.comment: In place of the CPU temperature: the program is automatic and none is running

data.name: CpuTemperature_StartHWiNFO
data.value: Start HWiNFO with shared memory to see it
data.comment: In place of the CPU temperature: HWiNFO is chosen and is not running

data.name: CpuTemperature_StartAfterburner
data.value: Start MSI Afterburner to see it
data.comment: In place of the CPU temperature: MSI Afterburner is chosen and is not running

data.name: CpuTemperature_StartLibreHardwareMonitor

data.comment: In place of the CPU temperature: LibreHardwareMonitor is chosen and its web server does not answer

data.value: Windows does not report it: choose a sensor program in the settings
data.comment: In place of the CPU temperature: the instance is set to Windows only

data.name: CpuTemperature_NotReported
data.value: The sensor program does not report it
data.comment: In place of the CPU temperature: the program runs but has none

data.name: Gpu_Asleep
data.comment: In place of the temperature of a graphics card that is powered off to save power

data.name: Settings_ProviderNote
data.value: The processor temperature comes only from a sensor program running beside the widget. The processor load and the graphics cards are taken from the program when it reports them, otherwise from Windows; all graphics cards come from one of the two. Memory and disks always come from Windows. Automatic uses the first program found: HWiNFO, then MSI Afterburner, then LibreHardwareMonitor.

data.name: Settings_HWiNFONote
data.value: In HWiNFO, turn on Shared Memory Support in its settings. The free version keeps it on for 12 hours, then it has to be turned on again.

data.name: Settings_AfterburnerNote
data.value: MSI Afterburner shares the graphs turned on on the Monitoring tab of its settings: turn on the temperature and usage of the CPU and the GPUs. It reports the CPU temperature not on every computer.

data.name: Settings_LibreHardwareMonitorNote
data.value: In LibreHardwareMonitor, start the web server: Options → Remote Web Server → Run. If its port was changed there or HTTP authentication turned on, enter the same here. The server is open to the local network: turn on authentication if the network is not only yours.

data.name: Settings_LibreHardwareMonitorUserName
data.value: User name, if authentication is on

data.name: Settings_LibreHardwareMonitorAddressInvalid
data.value: Enter the address of the web server, for example http://localhost:8085

data.name: Settings_SectionsNote
data.value: A section turned off is not read either.

data.name: Settings_ShowSystem
data.value: System: CPU, memory and video card load

data.name: Settings_ExternalDrives

data.name: Settings_DrivesNote
data.value: Drives turned off are not read: the widget does not reach for a network drive without a connection and does not wake a sleeping external disk.
